title: Serre duality for smooth proper curves
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a
proper smooth connected curve over $k$ and
$\mathcal M$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_C$-module (a
quasi-coherent module Zariski-locally isomorphic to
$\mathcal O_C^{\oplus r}$ for some $r\ge0$), with dual
$\mathcal M^{\vee}:=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_C)$.
Put $n:=\dim C\in\{0,1\}$ and $\omega_C:=\Omega^n_{C/k}$, where
$\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials of $C$
over $k$ ([def-sc-kahler-differentials]) and
$\Omega^0_{C/k}=\mathcal O_C$. Then all groups
$H^q(C,\mathcal M)$ and $H^q(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$
are finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces (coherent cohomology of a
proper scheme over a field is finite-dimensional: *Source:
Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1,
[Tag 02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)*), and
for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
H^q(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^{n-q}\bigl(C,\;\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\bigr)
$$

(both sides vanish unless $0\le q\le n$). In particular, for
$n=1$ and an invertible $\mathcal M$ ([def-sc-invertible-module],
so $\mathcal M^{\vee}\cong\mathcal M^{-1}$ by
[lem-sc-invertible-dual]):

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^0\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr),
\qquad
H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^1\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr).
$$

This is Serre duality $H^q(X,\mathcal F)^{\vee}\cong H^{n-q}(X,\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes\omega_X)$
for a smooth proper $X$ of dimension $n\le1$ over an algebraically
closed field and a finite locally free $\mathcal F$. For a coherent
$\mathcal F$ which is not locally free the right hand side must be
replaced by $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)$, as in
[thm-sc-p1-duality]: e.g. for the skyscraper
$\mathcal F=\kappa(x)$ at a closed point $x$ of a curve,
$H^0(C,\mathcal F)^{\vee}=k$ but $\mathcal F^{\vee}=0$.

proof.text:
The sheaf $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is a line bundle
([lem-sc-canonical-sheaf]), so $\omega_C$ is a line bundle and
$\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$ is finite locally free, by
trivializing both factors. Since $C$ is of finite type over the
Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, it is Noetherian by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. These finite locally free
sheaves are quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by
[pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] (01XZ). Apply
[lem-pc-coherent-hi] (02O5) to the proper morphism
$C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its coherent cohomology groups are
finite $k$-modules, hence finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces.

*Reduction to $q=n$.* For finite locally free $\mathcal M$ the
canonical maps $\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^{\vee\vee}$ and
$\omega_C^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\to\mathcal O_C$ are isomorphisms
(check on opens where the modules are free), so
$(\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\cong\mathcal M$.
Hence, once the isomorphism
$H^n(C,\mathcal N)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal N^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$
is proved for every finite locally free $\mathcal N$, applying it to
$\mathcal N:=\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$ gives
$H^n(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal M)$,
and dualizing (finite-dimensional spaces) gives the case $q=0$,
$H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\cong H^n(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$.
For $n=0$ the cases $q=0$ and $q=n$ coincide. It remains to show
the vanishing $H^q(C,\mathcal N)=0$ for $q\notin\{0,\dots,n\}$ and
every finite locally free $\mathcal N$ (for $q<0$ this is the
convention for derived functors), and the case $q=n$.

*Case $\dim C=0$.* This case cannot occur: by
[def-sc-curves], a connected curve is nonempty and has dimension
one. The $n=0$ assertions are therefore vacuous for the stated
hypotheses.

*Case $\dim C=1$.* The connected smooth curve $C$ is
integral: its local rings are domains ([lem-sc-smooth-regular]),
so its irreducible components are pairwise disjoint (a point
belonging to two components would have a local ring with two minimal
primes), and connectedness leaves a single component. Choose a
nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C$. Since $C$ is
an integral finite-type curve, $A$ is a finite-type domain over $k$
and $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=k(C)$ by [def-sc-function-field]; the same
holds for $\mathcal O_C(V)$ for every nonempty affine open $V\subset C$.
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] to each such
$\mathcal O_C(V)$: $\dim V=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(C)$, the same
number for all $V$. A chain $Z_0\subsetneq Z_1$ of irreducible closed
subsets of $C$ restricts to a chain of the same length in any affine
open $V$ meeting $Z_0$, so $\dim C=\sup_V\dim V$; as $\dim C=1$
([def-sc-curves]) we get $\dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(C)=1$, and
every maximal localization of $A$ has dimension one. Choose
$t\in k(C)\setminus k$ (transcendental since $k$ is algebraically
closed), and let $f:=\pi_t:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be the morphism of
[lem-sc-morphism-from-function]: finite, surjective and flat,
of degree $d:=[k(C):k(t)]$.

*Transfer of the cohomology.* The morphism $f$ is proper
(finite morphisms of schemes are proper,
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] of the ambient-foundations chapter), and its fibres
are finite ([pqf-lem-finite-qf] and
[pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] of the quasi-finite chapter); $\mathbf P^1_k$
is locally Noetherian (of finite type over the field $k$). Let
$\mathcal M$ be finite locally free. It is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], since $C$ is
locally Noetherian and $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, so [pqf-lem-fff-vanishing] gives
$(R^p f_*\mathcal M)_y=0$ for all $p>0$ and all
$y\in\mathbf P^1_k$, i.e. $R^pf_*\mathcal M=0$ for $p>0$
([pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks]). The Leray spectral sequence
$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,R^qf_*\mathcal M)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathcal M)$
([pqf-lem-leray]) is therefore concentrated on the row $q=0$ and
degenerates, giving $H^p(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)$
for all $p$; in degree one this is the low-degree exact sequence of
[pqf-lem-leray-lowdegree]:

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M),
\qquad
H^p(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)=0\quad(p\ge2),
$$

the vanishing by [lem-sc-p1-hi-vanishing]. This is the vanishing
outside $\{0,1\}$ required in the reduction step.

Moreover $f_*\mathcal M$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module (of rank $rd$ if $\mathcal M$ has rank $r$): over an affine
open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset\mathbf P^1_k$ the preimage
$f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine with $B$ finite
and flat over the Noetherian ring $R$. Since a finite module over a
Noetherian ring is finitely presented, [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective]
shows that $B$ is finite projective over $R$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], the finite locally
free sheaf $\mathcal M|_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$ is the sheaf of
$P:=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal M)$. Since $\mathcal M$ is finite locally free, it is of finite
presentation and flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]
the module $P$ is finitely presented over $B$, while the section
localization formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]
identify its localizations with the free modules of the
trivializing opens. Thus $P$ is flat, as flatness of a module is
checked on localizations; [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective]
makes $P$ finite projective over $B$. As a direct summand of $B^{\oplus m}$, $P$ is then
finite projective over $R$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], there is a
standard-open cover of $U$ on which $P$ is finite free; by
[lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and
[lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module], the pushforward sheaf is
$\widetilde P$ and is free on those opens. Thus $f_*\mathcal M$ is
finite locally free. Its generic rank is $rd$, where
$d=\dim_{k(t)}k(C)$.

*Duality.* Since $f_*\mathcal M$ is finite locally free and
$\mathbf P^1_k$ is locally Noetherian, it is coherent by
[pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Then [thm-sc-p1-duality] gives

$$
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr),
$$

and since $f$ is finite flat, [lem-sc-finite-duality] gives

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
\cong
H^0\bigl(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee}\bigr).
$$

Composing (the three isomorphisms are compatible with the
identification $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$):

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
\cong H^0\bigl(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\Omega^1_{C/k}\bigr),
$$

which is the case $q=n=1$; by the reduction step this proves the
theorem. For invertible $\mathcal M$, [lem-sc-invertible-dual]
identifies $\mathcal M^{\vee}$ with $\mathcal M^{-1}$, which gives
the two displayed particular cases.

Supplies properness of the finite map to the projective line; the unit has no finite-morphism permanence result.
Identifies the finite map as quasi-finite for the cohomology transfer; the unit has no quasi-finite criterion.
Supplies finite fibres of the finite map for the higher-direct-image vanishing theorem.
Gives vanishing of higher direct images along the finite-fibre proper map; the unit does not prove this cohomological tool.
Turns stalkwise vanishing of higher direct images into sheaf vanishing.
Provides the Leray spectral sequence for transferring cohomology through the finite map.
Identifies H1 on the curve with H1 on the projective line after higher-direct-image vanishing.
Gives the projective-line higher-cohomology vanishing needed outside degrees zero and one.
Shows the canonical sheaf is a line bundle in step 1; the unit does not prove this curve geometry fact.
Shows the finite-type curve over a field is Noetherian for step 1.
Identifies finite locally free quasi-coherent modules with coherent modules on locally Noetherian schemes in steps 1, 5, and 6.
Gives finite-dimensional coherent cohomology for the proper curve over Spec k in step 1.
Its connected-curve convention excludes the dimension-zero case in step 3.
Compares dimension and transcendence degree of an affine chart in step 4.
Makes the finite flat affine algebra finite projective over the Noetherian base ring in step 5.
Identifies a quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme with the sheaf of its sections in step 5.
Provides a finite standard-open cover on which a finite projective module is free in step 5.
Identifies the sheaf of a free module with a free sheaf on affine opens in step 5.
Turns finite presentation of the locally free sheaf on Spec B into finite presentation of its section module in step 5.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $C$ a scheme over $k$ which is smooth of
relative dimension $1$ and proper over $k$, and let
$\omega_C:=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ be the sheaf of Kähler differentials of $C$
over $k$ ([def-sc-kahler-differentials]). For a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal M$ (a
quasi-coherent module Zariski-locally isomorphic to
$\mathcal O_C^{\oplus r}$ for some $r\ge0$) write
$\mathcal M^{\vee}:=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_C)$.
Then for $p,q\ge0$ with $p+q=1$ there are $k$-linear isomorphisms

$$
e_{\mathcal M}:H^q(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
H^{p}\bigl(C,\;\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\bigr),
$$

natural in $\mathcal M$: for every morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of finite locally free modules,
$e_{\mathcal M}\circ H^q(\varphi)^{\vee}
=H^p(\varphi^{\vee}\otimes1)\circ e_{\mathcal N}$. In particular, for
an invertible $\mathcal M$ ([def-sc-invertible-module],
so $\mathcal M^{\vee}\cong\mathcal M^{-1}$ by
[lem-sc-invertible-dual]):

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^0\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr),
\qquad
H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^1\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr).
$$

For a coherent
$\mathcal F$ which is not locally free the right hand side must be
replaced by $\operatorname{Ext}^{p}(\mathcal F,\omega_C)$, as in
[thm-sc-p1-duality]: e.g. for the skyscraper
$\mathcal F=\kappa(x)$ at a $k$-rational point $x$ of $C$,
$H^0(C,\mathcal F)^{\vee}=k$ but $\mathcal F^{\vee}=0$.

proof.text:
All modules below are finite locally free, hence coherent on the
Noetherian scheme $C$ ([pqf-def-coherent]); their cohomology groups are
finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, $C$ being proper over $k$.

**Step 1 (reduction to connected $C$).** The scheme $C$ is of finite type
over $k$, hence Noetherian, so it has finitely many connected components
$C_1,\dots,C_m$, each open and closed; $C=\coprod_jC_j$, and each $C_j$
is again smooth of relative dimension $1$ and proper over $k$. Restriction
to the $C_j$ identifies a finite locally free module $\mathcal M$ with the
family $(\mathcal M|_{C_j})_j$, morphisms with families of morphisms, and
$H^q(C,\mathcal M)=\bigoplus_jH^q(C_j,\mathcal M|_{C_j})$, naturally in
$\mathcal M$; moreover $(\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)|_{C_j}=
(\mathcal M|_{C_j})^{\vee}\otimes\omega_{C_j}$, since duals, tensor
products and Kähler differentials are formed locally. Since
$(\bigoplus_jV_j)^{\vee}=\bigoplus_jV_j^{\vee}$ for finitely many
$V_j$, natural isomorphisms $e^{(j)}$ on the components assemble to
$e_{\mathcal M}:=\bigoplus_je^{(j)}_{\mathcal M|_{C_j}}$, natural in
$\mathcal M$. So we may assume $C$ connected (if $C=\emptyset$ all groups
are $0$).

**Step 2 (reduction to $q=1$).** The sheaf $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is a line
bundle ([lem-sc-canonical-sheaf]; it is locally free of rank $1$ because
$C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$), so
$\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$ is again finite locally free (on an
open trivializing $\mathcal M$ and $\omega_C$ it is $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$).
For finite locally free $\mathcal M$ the canonical maps
$\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^{\vee\vee}$ and
$\omega_C^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\to\mathcal O_C$ are isomorphisms
(check on opens where the modules are free), so there is an isomorphism
$\beta_{\mathcal M}:(\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\cong\mathcal M$,
natural in $\mathcal M$. Suppose the case $q=1$ is proved: natural
isomorphisms $e^1_{\mathcal N}:H^1(C,\mathcal N)^{\vee}\cong
H^0(C,\mathcal N^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$ for finite locally free
$\mathcal N$. Applying $e^1$ to $\mathcal N:=\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$
and composing with $H^0(\beta_{\mathcal M})$ gives an isomorphism
$H^1(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal M)$,
natural in $\mathcal M$ (both $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$
and $\beta$ are natural). Dualizing, and using that a finite-dimensional
space is naturally isomorphic to its bidual, gives
$e^0_{\mathcal M}:H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\cong H^1(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$,
natural in $\mathcal M$: the case $q=0$, $p=1$.

**Step 3 (a finite flat map to $\mathbf P^1_k$).** Let $C$ be connected.
Then $C$ is integral: its local rings are domains
([lem-sc-smooth-regular]), so its irreducible components are pairwise
disjoint (a point belonging to two components would have a local ring
with two minimal primes), and connectedness leaves a single component.
It is nonempty of dimension $1$ (smooth of relative dimension $1$), so
its function field $k(C)$ ([def-sc-function-field]) has transcendence
degree one over $k$: for an integral scheme of finite type over a field,
$\dim X=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(X)$ by Noether normalization (as in the
proof of [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero]). The generic stalk of the line
bundle $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is $\Omega^1_{k(C)/k}$, a one-dimensional
$k(C)$-vector space spanned by the differentials $dt$, $t\in k(C)$;
choose $t\in k(C)$ with $dt\neq0$. Then $t$ is transcendental over $k$:
since $C$ is smooth, hence geometrically reduced, over $k$, every element
of $k(C)$ algebraic over $k$ is separable over $k$, and a separable
algebraic element $a$ has $da=0$ (differentiate its minimal polynomial
$P$: $P'(a)\,da=0$ with $P'(a)\neq0$). Moreover $k(C)$ is finite over
$k(t)$ (finitely generated of transcendence degree one) and
$\Omega^1_{k(C)/k(t)}=\Omega^1_{k(C)/k}/k(C)\,dt=0$, so the finite
extension $k(C)\supset k(t)$ is separable. Let
$f:=\pi_t:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be the morphism of
[lem-sc-morphism-from-function]: finite, surjective and flat, of degree
$d:=[k(C):k(t)]$.

**Step 4 (transfer of the cohomology).** The morphism $f$ is proper
(finite morphisms of schemes are proper, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper])
with finite fibres ([pqf-lem-finite-qf], [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]), and
$\mathbf P^1_k$ is locally Noetherian. Let $\mathcal M$ be finite locally
free, hence coherent ([pqf-def-coherent]). Then [pqf-lem-fff-vanishing]
gives $(R^pf_*\mathcal M)_y=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $y\in\mathbf P^1_k$,
i.e. $R^pf_*\mathcal M=0$ for $p>0$ ([pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks]). The
Leray spectral sequence
$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,R^qf_*\mathcal M)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathcal M)$
([pqf-lem-leray]) is therefore concentrated on the row $q=0$ and gives
isomorphisms $H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)\cong H^p(C,\mathcal M)$, the
edge maps, which are natural in $\mathcal M$; in degree one this is the
low-degree exact sequence of [pqf-lem-leray-lowdegree]:
$H^1(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)$.

Moreover $f_*\mathcal M$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module: over an affine open
$U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset\mathbf P^1_k$ the preimage
$f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine with $B$ a finite locally
free $R$-algebra (finite flat), and $f_*\mathcal M|_U$ is associated with
$\Gamma(f^{-1}(U),\mathcal M)$, a finitely generated projective
$B$-module, hence a finitely generated projective $R$-module (a direct
summand of $B^{\oplus m}$, which is finite projective over $R$); if
$\mathcal M$ has rank $r$, its rank is $rd$.

**Step 5 (duality, $q=1$).** Since $f_*\mathcal M$ is coherent,
[thm-sc-p1-duality] gives an isomorphism
$H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1})$,
and since $f$ is finite flat with $k(C)\supset k(t)$ separable,
[lem-sc-finite-duality] gives
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1})\cong
H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee})$. Composing,

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
\cong H^0\bigl(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\Omega^1_{C/k}\bigr).
$$

Each of the three isomorphisms is natural in $\mathcal M$: the first is
the dual of the Leray edge isomorphism applied to the morphisms
$f_*\varphi$; the second is the canonical duality isomorphism of
[thm-sc-p1-duality], natural in the coherent module $\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal M$;
the third is composed of the adjunction
$\operatorname{Hom}(f_*\mathcal M,\mathcal G)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal M,\mathcal Hom(f_*\mathcal O_C,\mathcal G))$,
natural in $\mathcal M$, the fixed trace identification
$\mathcal Hom(f_*\mathcal O_C,\omega_{\mathbf P^1})\cong f_*\omega_C$, and
the natural isomorphism
$\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee}\cong\mathcal Hom(\mathcal M,\omega_C)$.
This is the case $q=1$, $p=0$; with Steps 1 and 2 the theorem follows.
For invertible $\mathcal M$, [lem-sc-invertible-dual] identifies
$\mathcal M^{\vee}$ with $\mathcal M^{-1}$, which gives the two displayed
particular cases.
